note: The OLG's SNAP Attributed Amount (Riverside Rule) page thoroughly covers the core FNS 1080 mandatory requirement: SNAP benefits must not increase when cash assistance under a means-tested program is reduced or suspended due to non-compliance. The OLG explains the mechanism (Attributed Amount added as unearned income), lists specific TAFDC and EAEDC sanction triggers, documents duration rules, and confirms BEACON automation. However, the OLG does not mention the FNS optional provision allowing states to reduce the SNAP allotment by up to 25% — Massachusetts appears to have chosen not to exercise this option, using the Attributed Amount mechanism instead, but the OLG does not document this policy choice. Additionally, FNS 1080 explicitly distinguishes means-tested programs from non-means-tested ones (RSDI, Railroad Retirement, Unemployment Compensation); the OLG handles this only by reference to 106 CMR 360.030(G) without explaining the distinction or listing excluded programs. The CMR at 363.220(C)(5) confirms MA's implementation aligns with the mandatory FNS requirement and adds conditions (good faith effort to obtain information, adjusting benefits for added eligible members, adjusting for unrelated household changes) not mentioned in FNS 1080.
